text: What keeps breaking the internet's undersea cables? It isn't sharks.
Between 2007 and 2014, fish bites, sharks included, caused exactly zero cable faults.
Yet there are a hundred and fifty to two hundred faults every year, worldwide.
Seventy to eighty percent of them are us: fishing gear and ships' anchors, dragged across a cable by accident.
Out in the deep, the cable is about as thick as a garden hose, lying on the sea floor.
So when one breaks out there, how do you fix it?
The answer involves a hook. It's level seven of the full video, linked below.
